http://www.htpcguides.com/install-nzbdrone-ubuntu/

Linux and Sonarr are the biggest pieces. NZBGet is for getting your files via Usenet server. You can use a Torrent program instead, but I like Usenet for pure speed.

I added VMWare to a local box and put two VM's of Linux on it. One purely for Plex (Video streaming server), and one for the rest, because VPN activated didn't allow Plex to work outside my home network. If that doesn't matter to you, then you can put it all on the same thing.

You will need a VPN service (like $30 a year), so you're less likely to get caught.

Plex is the video streamer, and the Roku box is what you hook your TV up to, and you get the Plex software on it, and stream from the Plex server to your TV.

So

Linux - Foundation Sonarr - Indexes, and categorizes shows NZBGet/Torrent - Program that grabs your shows VPN - routes your traffic around the world to hide yourself. Plex - Streams your media to various devices that has the Plex software on it (Phone, computer, Roku box, etc) Roku - Streaming box that pulls video/music from your Plex server to your TV.
